title: Interaction Antfarm — stress & fidelity probe notes
content:
Goal: sketch a lightweight feature + experiment harness that can simulate many small, realistic user interactions concurrently (the 'antfarm') so we can validate routing, fallback, batch sizing and cost/fidelity tradeoffs before shipping reroute or QoS rules.

Problem space / why:
- We have heuristics (priority routing, QoS lanes, fallback model variants) but limited ability to stress combinations of short sessions, high QPS spikes, and varying prefix cache locality.
- Current tests are either unit-level or large single-model load tests. Hard to reproduce realistic skew (thousands of 5–20 token turns, intermittent tool calls, quick terminations).

Nice-to-have outcomes:
- Deterministic repro of a scenario (seeded user traces).
- Fast DSL to express conversation archetypes (support small-turn bots, assistant flows, search-like prompts).
- Telemetry hooks that map to product metrics (latency P95, token cost per session, cold-starts, fallback frequency).
- Ability to inject network churn / capacity constraints.

Non-goals:
- Not a full chaos platform for infra (we can integrate with SRE chaos later).
- Not an A/B experiment runner; this is a pre-release validation harness.

MVP idea (minimal):
1) Small CLI tool + config file that launches N independent session-simulators. Each session is defined by a short trace template.
2) Templates: list of turns with optional wait times, optional tool-call events, and probabilistic branching (e.g., 80% follow-turn, 20% early-terminate).
3) Connects to hosted API endpoint with configurable routing headers (region, model-variant, session-id).
4) Emits structured events to stdout and to a telemetry stub (jsonlines file).

Example template (DSL sketch):
- name: "quick-help-bot"
  turns:
    - role: user
      text: "how do I reset password"
    - role: assistant
      action: generate
      latency_budget_ms: 200
    - role: user
      text: "thanks"
      probability: 0.6

User stories (MVP):
- As an SRE/PM I want to reproduce a workload of 5k small sessions/min with configurable burst shapes so I can verify autoscale and queueing behavior.
- As a Product engineer I want to run a curated set of session archetypes (search, chat-slim, stepper) and get a report of fallback counts and token cost so I can tune routing policies.
- As a Performance engineer I want to run the antfarm with different kv-cache-hit rates (0%, 30%, 70%) to measure token-per-response improvements.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Tool can generate 1k concurrent simulated sessions from a single laptop/cloud worker (or via k8s job).
- Generates telemetry that maps to: requests/sec, P50/P95 latency, token consumption, fallback events, model-variant used.
- Config file supports randomization seed and branching probabilities so tests are reproducible.

Success metrics (for using antfarm to validate a rollout):
- Able to detect a regression in P95 latency > 15% across a deployment change.
- Identify at least one routing policy misconfiguration that causes > 5% surge in fallback frequency during a simulated peak.

Instrumentation / telemetry plan (quick):
- Event schema: timestamp, session_id, trace_name, turn_index, event_type (request/response/fallback/tool-call), model_variant, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hit (y/n), error_code.
- Output: jsonl + optional push to dev observability namespace (low retention).

Quick rollout / experiment playbook:
- Step 0: run baseline profile against stable prod-model (night window) to capture typical metrics.
- Step 1: define scenario: 80% quick-help, 15% multi-turn task, 5% tool-heavy. Seed = 42.
- Step 2: run antfarm with routing policy A, collect telemetry, compare to baseline.
- Step 3: switch to routing policy B (e.g., cheaper-variant fallback enabled) and run same seed. Evaluate cost delta and regressions per-session.

Open questions / risks: 
- Partial compliance with production auth/quotas: must ensure we can run high-volume tests without interfering with real customers. Proposal: dedicated dev project + quota bucket.
- Privacy: sample text may contain PII in real traces; ensure synthetic templates by default.
- Interaction with token billing: ensure tests use earmarked test credits or count towards a separate billing view.

Experiment ideas / knobs to sweep:
- kv-cache-hit ratio (0–90%)
- average turn length (3–40 tokens)
- tool-call frequency (0–30%)
- model variant mix (% to cheap-quantized model)
- routing backpressure threshold to trigger fallbacks

MVP checklist (manual):
- [ ] DSL config parser (yaml/json)
- [ ] Session runner with concurrency control (worker pool)
- [ ] HTTP client with pluggable headers for routing flags
- [ ] JSONL telemetry writer + small analyzer script (python)
- [ ] Example scenario templates (3) + README

Longer-term ideas (notes-to-self):
- UI to build scenarios visually in Console -> 'Simulations' tab, with playback + diffing vs baseline.
- Integrate with canary flow: auto-run antfarm as part of canary window and block if regressions detected.
- Extend to Dedicated/Private: ability to run network-shim to exercise VPC routes and private endpoints.

Housekeeping / links to follow up:
- Slack thread: #perf-simulations (ask SRE about dedicated dev project).
- Linear ticket to create a cheap model-variant for synthetic tests: RED-3310.
- Prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/antfarm-sim (start branch: quick-mvp).

Notes-to-self for next session:
- Keep templates small and synthetic to avoid quota fallout.
- Add synthetic tool-call stubs (no real outbound requests).
- Make analyzer compute per-session cost and bucket by scenario.

Rough timeline (solo prototype):
- 1 week: CLI + templates + jsonl writer + one scenario runner.
- 2 weeks: telemetry mapping + analyzer + 3 scenarios.
- 4 weeks: integrate with small k8s job manifest and run 5k sessions/min smoke.

Random ideas:
- 'antcount' metric = average # of times a session triggered fallback per 1000 sessions.
- Embed a tiny primer generator to convert product flows into templates automatically from sample logs (redacted).

End of notes.

-- daphne
